alex: @here quick heads-up — saw a ~10-15% p99 regression on staging after the last runtime tweak. nsys trace looks weird: GPU compute time flat but queue time doubled when fanout > 12. attaching summary below

alex: ```
nsys timeline (top lines):
Time(ms) Kernel                 Duration(us)
0.0       cutlass_gemm_v2       2500
2.6       cudaMemcpyAsync       1200  <-- many small host->device memcpy spikes
5.0       dispatch_kernel       800
6.2       cutlass_gemm_fallback 300
Queue time (per-request) increased from ~1.2ms -> ~3.8ms in heavy load
```

maria: do we still use round-robin kernel_affinity for fanout? could be creating FIFO buildup across submission threads :thinking:

joel: my hunch is batching heuristic in continuous mode. when window grows we split into microbatches and fanout earlier -> more host submissions and memcpy contention. perfetto showed a hot 'submit_loop' on CPU.

sam: which model / seq len? nvprof counters?

alex: model=redwood-micro-1 (q4), seq=512 for the failing runs. nvprof snapshot shows long cudaMemcpy stall times on stream 7, kernel-launch latency normal. perfetto flame (sample):

alex: ```
perfetto (proc samples):
submit_loop           60% CPU
cudaMemcpy            18% CPU
kernel_launch         12% CPU
other_syscalls        10%
```

perf-bot: uploaded run bundle -> /runs/2311/nsys-231111.tar.gz (manual fetch) :eyes:

maria: another angle — kernel selection changed last week to prefer cutlass v2 path with small-GEMM fallback. that yields many smaller kernels + extra memcpy between launches. also check KV cache warmup: if we miss in KV cache we do extra host <-> device copies to materialize the cache entries.

joel: repro plan: force single-GPU affinity (no fanout) + usual load, and limit batch-window to 8ms. if p99 falls back to baseline -> clearly fanout/host contention.

alex: quick experiment results: single-gpu affinity -> p99 returns to baseline. limiting window to 8ms reduces queue spikes but throughput drops ~6%. so it's a tradeoff.

sam: sounds actionable. could we tweak the batch-slicer heuristic: prefer local accumulation until either wait_time > X ms OR pending_queue_size > Y, then fanout? that should reduce host submission storms while preserving throughput in spikey load.

maria: I'll draft a tiny heuristic PR + perf test (unit + nsys CI sampling). tagging @eng-runtime-owners for review. also adding a continuous nsys sampling job on canaries to catch queue-time regressions automatically.

alex: thanks. follow-ups: 1) test KV cache miss-paths to ensure no extra memcpy noise, 2) add a metric for host-submission-rate (submits/s) in console, 3) validate cutlass fallback thresholds produce fewer tiny kernels.

sam: agree. if anyone wants the raw traces I left the nsys short-link in the run bundle.

maria: will update thread when PR is up. :thumbsup:
